task: Independent supplemental review of existing host_session_offline_v1 against actual one-shot Host and persistent kernel lifecycle; not a replacement design.
verdict: Existing smallest offline scope is coherent. Three API/test details below remain to be made explicit; this review does not approve execution, production changes, XRT integration, or platform completion.

review_boundaries.commands_executed: Read-only source inspection and lightweight hashing/artifact serialization only.
review_boundaries.dependency_state: No board/XRT/platform capability claimed. Missing-dependency observations are inherited documented evidence; no duplicate environment probe was run.
review_boundaries.historical_text: Old 04934 resource statements and earlier claims of resident model upload are historical; actual one-shot Host and current Stage 5 header control this review.

verified_correspondence.item: 13 persistent BOs and model once per successful Session initialization
verified_correspondence.assessment: Existing run_host allocates all 13 once per invocation and uploads five once per invocation; a process/session lifetime change is still future work. Protocol event counts can test planned reuse without pretending actual XRT transfer occurred.

Keep all seven original allocation extents, whole-buffer zero/H2D each request, and full 32768 B IO zero/H2D. Smaller FullMemory accessible extents in laya_forward_full.cpp are not permission to shrink Host allocation or transfer contracts.

Actual code verifies exact five filenames/sizes/hashes, source SHA, four compiled tags, and AUX header. Per-file SHA is checked before its upload sync; AUX structural check follows all uploads but precedes first launch. Ready must only become observable after all initialization checks complete.

The proposed nonzero, nondecreasing generation and strictly increasing same-generation request ID match the kernel parser. New generation may start at any nonzero ID. Host ledger must distinguish submitted identity from kernel last_accepted identity, retain failed submitted IDs, and leave purely local preflight rejects unconsumed.

FullRuntime is static across invocations. full_recycle_request refuses FILL/READ/EXCLUSIVE_RW/DRAIN or outstanding readers, invalidates cache metadata, and preserves epoch high-water marks. Host workspace zeroing cannot reset on-chip ownership; Host must not invent BufferRef epochs or claim a higher generation forcibly cancels live owners.

verified_correspondence.item: Accepted kernel error versus transport failure
verified_correspondence.assessment: Controller attempts owner cleanup before committing an accepted error frame; cleanup failure returns without a new result header, and per-request IO zeroing allows Host validation to detect this. Existing CPU tests cover one accepted numerical failure and recovery, not arbitrary XRT abort. Valid identity-matched error frames may be delivered as errors and followed by a new identity; malformed/stale/absent frames poison the session.

Existing Host wait/readback/codec/identity/finite checks provide the intended ingredients. The old CLI writes the raw file before validating it; persistent API must distinguish raw diagnostics from validated delivery, as current design already requires. Shared decoder checks reserved bytes, counts, flags, unused B1 outputs, and error payload zeroing; separate finite checks remain necessary.

Default-off real XRT target requires actual headers/library and generated package. Protocol-only core must remain separate, with no stubs satisfying that target. group_id derives actual memory grouping; listed HBM banks remain candidates.

frozen_bo_contract.binding_note: Package was read for generated sizes/tags only; this review did not rehash the five 448923648 B model binaries.

specific_review_findings.priority: P1 implementation invariant, not a demonstrated bug in an unwritten core
specific_review_findings.title: Separate logical Poisoned state from whether device ownership has ended
specific_review_findings.source: design.md:13-17 and actual host/laya_host.cpp:426-440, main exception unwinding
specific_review_findings.issue: The prose correctly forbids release before a confirmed terminal state, but a four-state enum alone cannot distinguish Poisoned with confirmed completion from Poisoned while start/wait/abort has thrown and device activity is unknown. Copying existing exception unwinding into a resident adapter would destroy BO-owning objects without proving quiescence.
specific_review_findings.minimal_resolution: Freeze an orthogonal terminal/quiescence fact or equivalent explicit ownership token in the portable API. Set ownership conservatively before a start that can submit then throw. Enter Poisoned on transport/sync exceptions and unknown acceptance; never auto-retry. close/destruction must not emit BO release while ownership is uncertain. A confirmed terminal can allow resource cleanup according to the later pinned XRT contract, but never returns this first-version poisoned session to Ready.
offline_acceptance: Inject start submission followed by throw, wait throw, abort throw, and abort nonterminal/unknown.
Request close/destruction after each; event ledger must show no BO rewrite, new start, release, or return to Ready until terminal/quiescence is explicitly proven.
Exercise timeout then abort COMPLETED and timeout then ABORT: caller still receives timeout and session remains poisoned.
specific_review_findings.scope: This refines the already documented ownership requirement; no XRT recovery API or online reset implementation is requested.

specific_review_findings.title: Require exactly 384 result bytes at the portable transport boundary
specific_review_findings.issue: decode_result rejects fewer than 384 bytes but accepts trailing bytes. The current real Host is safe on this point because it always reads a fixed 384-byte array; a generic vector-returning test/backend API must preserve that exact-length contract explicitly.
specific_review_findings.minimal_resolution: Use an exact-size result frame type or require returned byte count == kResultBytes before decode_result. Retain strict request_frame.size == request.frame_bytes.
offline_acceptance: Reject result lengths 0, 383, and 385 with no accepted delivery; accept a separately frozen valid 384 B vector.
Keep raw malformed bytes diagnostic-only and poison the session after a malformed completed result.
specific_review_findings.scope: No shared codec or production Host change is required for this offline core.

specific_review_findings.title: Define identity exhaustion without unsigned wraparound
specific_review_findings.issue: The monotonic rule is sound, but the planned matrix omits UINT64_MAX boundaries. Any convenience increment in a future ledger/CLI could wrap to zero or incorrectly reopen an old generation.
specific_review_findings.minimal_resolution: Compare supplied uint64 identities directly; do not silently rewrite them. At request_id max, only a supplied higher nonzero generation can permit another request. At generation max there is no higher generation; same-generation larger ID remains legal only while one exists. Once both values are max, no next request exists in that session. Recovery/new session must not assume kernel state reset merely because Host objects were reconstructed.
offline_acceptance: Accept ID max once, reject same-generation reuse/zero, and accept ID 1 only with an available larger supplied generation.
Reject generation decrease and overflow-to-zero; exhaust (generation max, request_id max) without incrementing wrapped counters.
specific_review_findings.scope: No new ID allocator or tokenizer is required.

smallest_offline_evidence_matrix.assertions: 13 allocations and five model uploads once per successful session; two serial valid requests produce two workspace clears/H2D of 192937984 B, two 32768 B IO H2D, two starts/waits, two 384 B D2H; exact BO indices/order retained. These are event assertions only.

Bad tags/header/offset/padding/shape/payload size and duplicate/decreasing identities produce no request BO mutation/sync/start and consume no submitted identity. A second submission during an active request is rejected without device events.

Frozen B2 then B1 success, stale identity, different B/S, malformed result length, reserved/count/flags inconsistency, nonzero unused B1 lanes, NaN/Inf, and valid zero-payload nonOK frame. Only completed+synced+validated frames are delivered; valid errors retain status/detail/counters and are not success.

Fault injection before/after possible start, each wait/abort outcome and exception, result sync/readback failure, timeout-abort race, late stale completion, attempted close/destructor while uncertain, and any submission after Poisoned. Test event order and absence of forbidden release/reuse, not only final enum.

Model/init-validation failure never reaches Ready or permits start; partial allocation/upload is not reported as a successfully resident model. No protocol test claims actual SHA scanning unless that code is actually included and exercised.

Use exact frozen request/result bytes with named profile, package/build identity and fixture hashes plus independent byte-order vectors; do not generate all expected frames with the same codec under test. Pre-existing zero-tag reference-only requests must be rejected under current expected identity.

remaining_integration_gaps_not_offline_b: Current source compiles package tags and verifies an independently provided xclbin SHA, but no checked deployment record currently binds that xclbin SHA to the four tags, kernel name/argument metadata, selected platform/shell, and Host build. Preserve this as a required future deployment binding; fake backend events cannot prove it.

Explicitly select LAYA_FULL_MODEL_DIR=build/model-attention-rtl-repair-20261008 when current fe067 identity is intended. Existing CMake default build/model-repair is historical; a default directory must not silently choose the evaluated package.

Real XRT compile/link and version-specific wait/abort/destructor semantics, actual xclbin reload/reset and HBM retention, device exclusivity, group mapping and parameter metadata need pinned platform evidence later. The present source comment that abort is synchronous is not a board verification result.

CPU owner recovery evidence and protocol event backend cannot establish RTL AXI response drain at ap_done, asynchronous cancel quiescence, cache reset or HBM retention. Higher generation is not a replacement for terminal/quiescence confirmation.

A protocol-only core need not extract the production manifest/SHA/OpenSSL implementation now. Report initialization validation as an external attested/preconditioned step if it is not executed by that core, and test failed attestation explicitly.
No tokenizer redesign, network service, business decoding, production adapter, workspace-clear elimination, or performance claim is part of this independent review.

timing_contract.cold_initialization: Monotonic Host time from beginning deployment/package validation through device/kernel setup, 13 BO allocation, model read/hash/upload and Ready. If cold first response is reported, separately add the first full request and label that endpoint.
timing_contract.resident_kernel_host_observed: Immediately before kernel submission/start through observed COMPLETED. Includes Host/XRT dispatch/wait overhead; never label this hardware-only cycles.
timing_contract.resident_preencoded_request: Frame availability/admission through workspace/IO preparation and sync, start/wait, result D2H and validation/delivery. Keep 184 MiB workspace cost visible. This excludes tokenization/business decoding and therefore is not the complete service metric.
timing_contract.resident_full_host_request_future: Raw input preparation/tokenization through synchronization, kernel, readback, validation and actual business postprocessing. Mission Stage 5 full-service metric remains pending until these stages exist.
timing_contract.hardware_cycles: Read and label only valid counter scope; current full_result leaves prewrite_cycles/counter_scope and cycles_valid absent. Zero means unavailable here, not a zero-cycle kernel.
timing_contract.reporting: Later use warmup/sample count, P50/P95, B/S/candidate count, errors and throughput with B1/B2 separated; keep cold/per-request/model upload scopes distinct. Fake-backend wall time is not Host/device performance, and historical A6000 BF16 B2/S94/K_pad3 data is not a same-contract acceleration baseline.
